mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in >60% of 20-day periods following a sustained 3-month FEDFUNDS decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden 10% increase in PAYEMS (labor demand) within a month predicts stronger labor market confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 10% in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in >70% of 5-day periods following a PAYEMS spike >10%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO (supply index) for three consecutive months indicates weakening demand pressures, reducing inflation expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in >50% of 20-day periods following a sustained 3-month INDPRO rise.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in GDPC1 (demand) over the prior month signals coordinated monetary easing and strong demand, amplifying equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns in the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS down 1% and GDPC1 up 2% in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in >80% of 5-day periods when the combo occurs.

mechanism_narrative: In periods where FEDFUNDS remain below 1.5% for 4 months, a sustained 2% decline in FEDFUNDS over the next month predicts stronger equity market gains due to reduced policy tightness, leading to significantly higher S&P 500 returns than in other regimes over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly higher than baseline (p >0.05) in >60% of 20-day periods when FEDFUNDS <1.5% for 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE (labor cost pressures) and increase in PAYEMS (labor demand) above their 5-week moving averages signals conflicting labor trends, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE up 0.5% and PAYEMS up 5% above 5-week MA in prior month
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in >70% of 20-day periods when the combo occurs.

mechanism_narrative: During periods where UNRATE exceeds 7% for the prior month, a sharp increase in UNRATE predicts labor market instability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to concerns about economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly negative (p >0.05) in >80% of 5-day periods when UNRATE >7% for the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO (supply index) for four consecutive months indicates weakening demand pressures, reducing inflation expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in >50% of 60-day periods following a sustained 4-month INDPRO rise.
